samasa.type: bahuvrīhi, containing a tṛtīyā tatpuruṣa (भक्तिनम्र = भक्त्या नम्रः) and a ṣaṣṭhī tatpuruṣa (आत्ममूर्ति = आत्मनः मूर्तिः)
samasa.literal: they whose own bodies were bent by devotion
samasa.sense: the sages, bowing low in devotion

samasa.type: ṣaṣṭhī tatpuruṣa (अमर itself न म्रियते इति, ‘undying’)

morph.note: Perfect 3rd plural of √स्तु: reduplication तु- with the root’s s made ṣ after the reduplicating u (तु-ष्टु-), and u → uv before the ending -उः.
The enclitic pronoun एन- is used only for a person or thing already named (anvādeśa): ‘her’, the Goddess of 2.34.
Absolutive of √दृश् (ś + tvā → ṣṭvā). Its subject is the subject of the main verb: the asuras saw, and then rose (2.36).

mantras.anvaya: भक्तिनम्रात्ममूर्तयः मुनयः च एनां तुष्टुवुः। अमरारयः समस्तं त्रैलोक्यं संक्षुब्धं दृष्ट्वा (2.36: सन्नद्धाखिलसैन्याः समुत्तस्थुः)।
mantras.anvaya_en: The first line closes the scene of praise. The second line starts a new sentence: the absolutive clause with its subject अमरारयः, whose main verb comes in 2.36.
mantras.lit: And the sages, their own bodies bowed with devotion, praised her. Having seen the whole three worlds agitated, the enemies of the immortals —
mantras.tr: The sages, bowing low in devotion, sang her praise. But the enemies of the gods, seeing the three worlds in turmoil,
mantras.tr_note: ‘But’ marks the change of scene, which the Sanskrit makes by a new subject; the sentence continues into 2.36.

comm.t: Two answers to the roar. The sages praise her with bowed bodies; the asuras, seeing the worlds in upheaval, prepare for war (2.36). The same event is heard as grace by the one side and as threat by the other.
A modern reflection: the verse sets reverence and alarm side by side as responses to one and the same power. What a person sees in an upheaval says something about where they stand.

Visarga after u before a vowel appears as r.

Final t → d before a vowel.

samasa.type: bahuvrīhi (अखिल itself a nañ bahuvrīhi, न विद्यते खिलम् यस्य, ‘without remainder’)
samasa.literal: they whose entire armies were girded
samasa.sense: with their whole forces armed and in array

samasa.type: bahuvrīhi (prādi type: the prefix उद् stands for उद्यत ‘raised’)

samasa.sense: the asura who has the form of a buffalo
samasa.alt: Also read as a madhyamapadalopin karmadhāraya, महिषरूपः असुरः ‘the asura in buffalo form’; the sense is the same.

morph.note: Perfect of √स्था (reduplicated त-स्थ्-, the s dropped in the reduplicating syllable) with सम् + उद्. उद् + स्था loses its s (उत्था-), so the d of उद् appears as t: सम्-उत्-तस्थुः.
Absolutive with a prefix takes -य (lyap), not -त्वा: आ + √भाष् → आभाष्य ‘having called out’.

mantras.anvaya: (अमरारयः) ते सन्नद्धाखिलसैन्याः उदायुधाः समुत्तस्थुः। महिषासुरः ‘आः, किम् एतत्’ इति क्रोधात् आभाष्य (2.37: … अभ्यधावत)।
mantras.anvaya_en: The first line completes 2.35b. The second gives Mahiṣāsura’s cry, quoted with इति, as an absolutive clause; his main verb is in 2.37.
mantras.lit: they, their entire armies armed, rose up with weapons raised. Having exclaimed in anger, ‘Ah! What is this?’, Mahiṣāsura —
mantras.tr: rose up, weapons raised, their whole army in arms. ‘Ha! What is this?’ cried Mahiṣāsura in fury,
mantras.tr_note: The absolutive आभाष्य (‘having exclaimed’) is rendered as a finite verb; the sentence runs on into 2.37.

comm.t: The asuras arm themselves, and Mahiṣāsura appears in the narrative for the first time in person, with an angry question: ‘What is this?’ He does not yet know what the sound is.

A modern reading: Mahiṣa meets the Goddess first as a disturbance to be put down — ‘What is this?’ — not as a power to be understood. The question is asked in anger, and anger does not wait for the answer.

The visarga of सः is dropped before a consonant.

samasa.type: bahuvrīhi (लोकत्रय a ṣaṣṭhī tatpuruṣa, लोकानां त्रयम्)
samasa.literal: she by whom the triad of worlds is pervaded
samasa.sense: filling the three worlds (with her light)

morph.note: Imperfect ātmanepada of √धाव् with अभि (augment a- after the prefix: अभि + अ + धावत → अभ्यधावत). With a goal in the accusative: ‘ran at, charged towards’.
Perfect of √दृश् with guṇa of the root vowel (दर्श्) and reduplication द-: ‘he saw’.

mantras.anvaya: (महिषासुरः) अशेषैः असुरैः वृतः तं शब्दम् अभ्यधावत। ततः सः त्विषा व्याप्तलोकत्रयां देवीं ददर्श।
mantras.anvaya_en: The first line gives Mahiṣāsura’s main verb (subject in 2.36); the second line is a new sentence whose object is described through 2.38–39a.
mantras.lit: rushed towards that sound, surrounded by all the asuras. Then he saw the Goddess, who pervaded the three worlds with her radiance,
mantras.tr: and charged towards the sound with all his asuras around him. Then he saw the Goddess, her radiance filling the three worlds,
mantras.tr_note: The second sentence continues through 2.38 into 2.39a, all describing the Goddess as he sees her.

comm.t: Mahiṣa runs towards the sound and only then sees its source. The description of her begins with the phrase used for the gods’ gathered light in 2.13 (व्याप्तलोकत्रयं त्विषा): the light that became her body still fills the worlds. The vision runs on through 2.38–39a.

sandhi.type: vowel sandhi inside a compound (guṇa and savarṇa-dīrgha); consonant sandhi inside the prefix
sandhi.note: a + u → o (किरीटोल्लिखित); a + a → ā (-ताम्बराम्). In उल्लिखित the d of उद् has become l before l (उद् + लिखित).

sandhi.type: vowel sandhi inside a compound (savarṇa-dīrgha); anusvāra
sandhi.note: a + a → ā; the final m becomes anusvāra before the dh of the next word.
The s of धनुस् becomes r before the voiced j.

samasa.literal: by the stepping-on of the feet
samasa.sense: by the weight of her tread

samasa.literal: she by whom the earth is bowed
samasa.sense: the earth sinking under her step

samasa.vigraha: किरीटेन उल्लिखितम् अम्बरं यया सा, ताम्
samasa.type: bahuvrīhi (किरीटोल्लिखित a tṛtīyā tatpuruṣa, किरीटेन उल्लिखितम्)
samasa.literal: she by whom the sky was scraped with the crown
samasa.sense: so tall that her diadem touched the sky

samasa.vigraha: क्षोभितानि अशेषाणि पातालानि यया सा, ताम्
samasa.literal: she by whom all the netherworlds were stirred
samasa.sense: shaking the underworlds to their depths

samasa.type: ṣaṣṭhī tatpuruṣa (धनुर्ज्या also a ṣaṣṭhī tatpuruṣa, धनुषः ज्या)
samasa.literal: by the sound of the string of the bow
samasa.sense: by the twang of her bowstring

morph.note: The stem भू ‘earth’ keeps its form at the end of a bahuvrīhi; before a vowel ending ū becomes uv (भुवम्), as in the simple noun (भुवम्, भुवि).
आक्रान्ति is an action noun (ktin) from आ + √क्रम् ‘to step upon’; its instrumental gives the cause of the earth’s bowing.

mantras.anvaya: (सः) पादाक्रान्त्या नतभुवं, किरीटोल्लिखिताम्बरां, धनुर्ज्यानिःस्वनेन क्षोभिताशेषपातालां तां (देवीं ददर्श)।
mantras.anvaya_en: All accusatives in apposition to देवीम् (2.37); each bahuvrīhi has its own instrumental of cause beside it.
mantras.lit: her by whose tread the earth was bowed, by whose crown the sky was scraped, by the twang of whose bowstring all the netherworlds were shaken —
mantras.tr: the earth bending beneath her tread, her crown grazing the sky, the twang of her bowstring shaking the underworlds to their depths,
mantras.tr_note: The verse continues the object of ददर्श (2.37); the next verse completes it.

comm.t: What Mahiṣa sees is the Goddess as large as the cosmos: her foot presses the earth, her crown touches the sky, and the sound of her bow reaches the netherworlds. The three levels of the world are each touched by her.

Purāṇic cosmology divides the world into the heavens above, the earth, and the pātālas below. The verse touches all three, so that before a blow is struck the asura sees that the one he means to fight is as wide as the world.

morph.note: Perfect ātmanepada of √वृत् with प्र: reduplicated व-वृत्-, ending -ए. ‘(The battle) began, set in’.
वि + √आप् (वि → व्य् before आ by yaṇ) with -य: ‘having filled, having spread over’.

mantras.anvaya: (सः) भुजसहस्रेण समन्तात् दिशः व्याप्य संस्थितां (तां देवीं ददर्श)। ततः तया देव्या (सह) सुरद्विषां युद्धं प्रववृते।
mantras.anvaya_en: The first line ends the description of the Goddess (object of ददर्श, 2.37). The second line is a new sentence; तया देव्या is the instrumental of the one fought against (सह is understood).
mantras.lit: standing, having pervaded the directions on every side with a thousand arms. Then the battle of the enemies of the gods with that Goddess began,
mantras.tr: standing with her thousand arms spread through every quarter. Then the battle began between the Goddess and the enemies of the gods,
mantras.tr_note: The second line continues into 2.40, which describes the battle.

comm.t: The vision is completed by her arms, a thousand of them, filling the directions; then the battle begins. ‘A thousand’ here means beyond counting, completing the vertical vastness of 2.38 with the horizontal.

The madhyama-carita dhyāna of the Gita Press pāṭha pictures Mahālakṣmī with eighteen objects in her hands; the text’s own vision here is of a thousand arms. The two do not compete: the dhyāna is a form for meditation, the verse a vision of her cosmic extent.
